records.text: St. Ursula Villa was privately funded and separate from St. Ursula Academy and the Catholic Church at the time, according to Candace Owens's research
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Ursula Academy. It's a privately owned and at first glance you would think it was a Catholic school, but actually despite its name, despite it being on the St. Ursula Academy property, it was not owned by the nuns as St. Ursula Academy was. St. Ursula Villa actually had private funding. It was completely ... separate from the Catholic Church at this time, from what I've been able to see.

verification.notes: St. Ursula Villa's official history confirms governance transferred to an independent board in the early 1990s, supporting organizational separation from St. Ursula Academy. But the school describes itself as an independent Catholic school in the Ursuline tradition, so saying it was separate from the Catholic Church is misleading; the private-funding claim was not independently established.
